Operate

Deployment

The project site, the hosted server, and the Worker.

Project Site (GitHub Pages)#

The static site in website/ is published to https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/ by .github/workflows/pages.yml.

  • A push to main runs the website tests, builds _site from website/, and deploys the artifact with actions/deploy-pages.
  • No site build output is committed; CI generates _site on every push.
  • workflow_dispatch republishes the site from the Actions tab without a code change.
  • Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source, so there is no gh-pages branch. Removing pages.yml stops all publishing and the site returns 404.
  • The github-pages environment only allows deployments from main.

Hosted MCP Server#

The server is deployed via Horizon Prefect, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

Test Chat (UI)#

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat

MCP Server Endpoint#

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp

[!IMPORTANT] Authentication is required to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client.

Hosted Studio#

The Living Studio SPA is deployed to Cloudflare Workers:

Environment URL
Production (main) https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/
Pull request preview Posted automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds as a PR comment

Production deploys on every push to main. The Worker is agentic-odi; keep name in wrangler.jsonc aligned with the Worker connected in the dashboard. Preview builds run for non-production branches and are ephemeral: the Cloudflare PR comment is the source of truth, so do not copy a preview URL into docs. The hosted UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the sidecar tunnel described below.

Component Visual Review (Chromatic)#

Every *.visual.test.tsx file in apps/studio renders one component state in a real Chromium browser. The Chromatic workflow (.github/workflows/chromatic.yml) runs those tests on every branch push and publishes the snapshots to Chromatic. Reviewers compare the pixels, approve or reject the change in Chromatic, and the approved build becomes the baseline for the next comparison.

Project setup#

The project is linked to alehar9320/agentic-odi (app id 6add05ad03e0b1f6aeda07ad), and the CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN repository secret holds its project token, so the workflow publishes with no manual step. The first build, published from the CLI, holds the two FailurePanel snapshots: build 1.

To rotate the token, generate a new one in Manage → Project token and run gh secret set CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN. No code change is involved.

What CI does#

Event Result
Push to any branch Captures the component states, publishes a build, reports its status against that commit
Push to main Same, and chromatic.config.json auto-accepts, so main becomes the baseline
Push from Dependabot Captures snapshots, skips the upload with a notice: Dependabot runs cannot read repository secrets
Pull request from a fork No build; the workflow runs in this repository and never sees a fork branch
Missing token in any other run The job fails rather than passing without publishing

The workflow triggers on push rather than pull_request, which is Chromatic's recommendation: GitHub builds pull_request runs from an ephemeral merge commit, so the diff would include everything merged into main since the branch point. Chromatic still reports its UI Tests status on the pull request that contains the commit.

To stop a visual change from merging before someone looks at it, add Visual tests (Chromatic) and Chromatic's UI Tests to the required status checks for main (Settings → Rules → Rulesets). Unreviewed changes then keep the pull request red until they are approved in Chromatic.

[!NOTE] apps/studio/package.json overrides the transitive storybook version that @chromatic-com/vitest pins, to a release without the dev-server advisory that npm audit reports as critical. This project never runs a Storybook dev server; the override only patches the archive build Chromatic does internally. Revisit it when the plugin adopts a newer Storybook.

Staying inside the free plan#

Chromatic bills tests × builds × browsers × viewports, and the free plan includes 5,000 billed snapshots per month with Chrome only. Three deliberate choices keep this project far below that ceiling:

Choice Where Why
Browser mode only picks up *.visual.test.tsx apps/studio/vitest.visual.config.ts The 29 jsdom unit tests never bill a snapshot; adding a component to visual review is one explicit new file.
One Chromium instance, one viewport same file No browser or viewport matrix multiplying each test.
Animations paused at their end frame same file (pauseAnimationAtEnd) Shimmer and fade-in components do not diff on capture timing.

Today that is 2 snapshots per build, one build per branch push, so the monthly allowance would cover ~2,500 builds. A component added to visual review costs one snapshot per state per build, so keep new files focused on the states that matter rather than every prop permutation.

apps/studio/chromatic.config.json auto-accepts changes on main (so the default branch updates its baseline without a manual review) and exits zero on visual changes elsewhere, so the job itself reports success while the review lands in Chromatic's UI Tests check. Rendering errors still fail the job.

Commands#

# Capture archives; needs Chromium locally (npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix apps/studio run test:visual

# Upload the archives captured above
CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN=... npm --prefix apps/studio run chromatic

Adding a component#

  1. Create apps/studio/src/components/<Name>.visual.test.tsx.
  2. Render the state you want reviewed, importing ../styles/theme.css so the snapshot uses the real theme.
  3. Call configure({ title: "<Name>" }) from @chromatic-com/vitest if the derived name is not the component name.
  4. Add one test per state worth reviewing. Automatic snapshots are captured at the end of each test; use takeSnapshot("name") for a mid-test state.

Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker#

Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies /api/* to the sidecar through a free, account-less Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.

wrangler.jsonc publishes apps/studio/dist with SPA fallback and runs the Worker first for /api/*; infra/cloudflare/worker.ts forwards those calls to the SIDECAR_URL secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the sidecar's CORS list is not involved.

# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
npm --prefix apps/studio ci
npm --prefix apps/studio run build

# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
python scripts/dev.py

# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints

# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
npx wrangler deploy

Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):

Setting Value
Production branch main
Root directory /
Build command npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build
Deploy command npx wrangler deploy
Preview command npx wrangler preview

A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set name in wrangler.jsonc to the Worker you created before the first deploy.

Pull request previews#

Workers Builds posts the build status and Preview URL to the pull request automatically. To enable it:

  1. Open the Worker → Settings → Build → Branch control.
  2. Keep the production branch set to main and enable Preview Builds.
  3. If Cloudflare shows Set up Worker Previews, complete the one-time switch. This cannot be reversed.
  4. Confirm the Preview command is npx wrangler preview.

wrangler.jsonc must keep a previews block, even an empty one: the wrangler preview command fails the build with "Your Wrangler configuration is missing a previews block" without it. Assets and compatibility settings stay at the top level, so "previews": {} is enough while Previews need no extra settings. If a future Preview needs vars or bindings, add them under previews with Preview-safe values.

Previews do not inherit production settings. The SPA loads from a Preview, but /api/* returns 502 SIDECAR_URL is not configured until a preview-specific SIDECAR_URL secret is configured:

npx wrangler preview secret put SIDECAR_URL --name <branch>

When --name is omitted it defaults to the current git branch. Previews are ephemeral, and pull requests from forks may not receive one. If Cloudflare does not comment, paste the URL into the PR's Deployment section.

The cf CLI can inspect build triggers and recent builds (cf builds triggers list, cf builds list) and create a Preview (cf previews deploy), but it does not post GitHub PR comments. The Workers Builds Git integration owns the PR link; cf is only an optional verification tool and requires cf auth login.

[!NOTE] The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while python scripts/dev.py and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs change on every restart — update the secret with npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL. Chat also needs a reachable OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's Settings; the canvas, job map, and impact simulation work without one.
